name: Ben-hur
overview: Ben-hur was a male figure known for serving as one of King Solomon's twelve deputies, specifically overseeing the region of Ephraim. His role as a deputy highlights his position of authority and responsibility during Solomon's reign. Beyond this notable office, Scripture provides limited additional personal details about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Ben-hur means 'son of Hur,' indicating a patronymic origin. This proper name, recorded in 1 Kings 4:8, does not appear to have been given by God but serves to identify him within the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Ben-hur beyond what is indicated by his name and his official role. There are no additional familial connections detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ben-hur's significance lies in his administrative role under King Solomon, representing the organized governance Solomon established over Israel. As one of the twelve deputies, his leadership in Ephraim contributed to the stability and management of the kingdom during a pivotal era in Israel's history. His mention underscores the structured delegation of authority in Solomon's government.
